name: pidfd_getfd
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_pidfd_getfd, int pidfd, int targetfd, unsigned int flags);
Note: glibc provides no wrapper for pidfd_getfd(), necessitating the use of syscall(2).
description: The pidfd_getfd() system call allocates a new file descriptor in the calling process, duplicating an existing file descriptor from another process. The new descriptor shares the same open file description as the original, including file status flags and offset. The flags argument must be 0 for now.

parameters.name: pidfd
parameters.description: File descriptor referring to the process whose file descriptor is to be duplicated.

parameters.name: targetfd
parameters.description: The file descriptor in the target process to duplicate.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Reserved for future use; must be specified as 0.

return_value.success: Returns a file descriptor (a nonnegative integer)
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: pidfd is not a valid PID file descriptor
targetfd is not an open file descriptor in the process referred to by pidfd
The per-process limit on the number of open file descriptors has been reached
The system-wide limit on the total number of open files has been reached
The calling process did not have the necessary permissions (PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH_REALCREDS)
The process referred to by pidfd does not exist
